summary: A skeleton iron tower at the southern tip of Point Loma, lit in 1891 to replace the fog-bound old lighthouse on the ridge; now Coast Guard property and closed to the public.

notes_for_editor: This record is the 1891 New Point Loma light; the 1855 station is us-ca-old-point-loma. Disagreements left in the text: electric lamp 1925 (Bulletin) vs 1933 (NPS, Lighthouse Friends); NPS page mentions first lighting on 3 Feb 1891 and 23 March in the same paragraph (Lighthouse Friends: 3 Feb was lens arrival); Cady's 1912 rescue details come only from Lighthouse Friends (the Bulletin gives one line); Israel's resignation story from Lighthouse Friends/NPS vs Holland (cause obscured). Lighthouse Friends gives Cottingham to 1934 and the Archive to 1935. No newspaper search completed (loc.gov search timed out), so the Cady and 1891 lighting accounts are unverified in contemporary papers. The 1896-97 report entry (barn, erosion) is cited to the volume; scan page not confirmed. The 1891-92 Board list shows the March date damaged by OCR. Holland says the site is about 30 ft above the sea while the Bulletin and Archive give the light at 88 ft; not reconciled in text. The Archive roster is used for names only and lists 29 Coast Guard names 1946-1969 with no roles. Tower height 21 m (70 ft) is from Lighthouse Friends; the Archive gives 60 ft from base to lantern centre. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Board report fiscal years corrected (cite 6 is FY1891, 7 is FY1892, 8 FY1894, 9 FY1896); the 1925 illuminant entry is in the June 1925 Bulletin issue; water-supply anecdote attributed to Joe Brennan's recollection quoted by Lighthouse Friends.
